Libya's Gharyan University signed a memorandum with Dassault Systemes and ABBK PhysicsWorks for SolidWorks licences and certification training at its Entrepreneurship and Innovation Centre, open to entrepreneurs and startup owners from inside and outside the university, reported 13 February 2026 citing the Ministry of Higher Education.

fact: The National Programme for Micro and Small Enterprises' technology incubator in Tripoli runs an incubation programme with training, incubation contracts, quarterly reviews and a possible launch grant for tech projects.

SPARK states that Silphium Labs, a business incubator founded with Omar Al-Mokhtar University and ION+ under the EU-funded Libya Startup Programme, took in Smart Tech in 2024 and ran a final pitching event in May 2025 awarding 15,000 euro seed funding.
Libya Herald reports Tripoli Business Hub, a municipal centre of Tripoli Central Municipality, officially opened on 11 March 2026 and will offer incubation programmes, with no cohort stated.
SPARK says the Silphium Labs incubator in Al-Bayda completed its second cohort, 21 of 228 applicants through a two-month programme with seed funding for top startups.
SPARK states the Asarya Business Incubator in Benghazi, founded January 2024, ran a six-month incubation for a cohort of 26 startups, closing 3 August 2024.

UNDP states the Tripoli Business Hub, Libya's first municipality-led business hub, officially opened on 10 August 2025 with EU and Italian support, and will offer co-working, mentorship and training for start-ups.
Tripoli Central Municipality inaugurated the city's first business incubator for startup entrepreneurs on 10 August 2025, with UNDP support; no programme or cohort is described.
